candidates.title: Rollups withdrawal path: validateAccount authenticates the zero-padded account bytes, so any zero-extended or zero-truncated variant of a committed account is accepted (lost length) and burns the account's single withdrawal
candidates.component: cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 pinned by Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 (dapp/Application.sol validateAccount / withdraw, library/LibBinaryMerkleTree.sol merkleRoot, library/LibKeccak256.sol hashBlock); deployed by Dave's DaveAppFactory with a WithdrawalConfig
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md component table: Dave and the cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 it pins)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/dapp/Application.sol: withdraw (~257-280), validateAccount (~405-418), validateAccountMerkleRoot (~420-438); src/library/LibBinaryMerkleTree.sol merkleRoot ('Data blocks are right-padded with zeros'); src/library/LibKeccak256.sol hashBlock (partial/absent blocks hashed as zero-filled); src/withdrawal/IWithdrawalOutputBuilder.sol (interface allows variable-size accounts: 'should validate its length (possibly raising an InvalidAccountSize error)', and fixes the owner as the LAST 20 bytes)
candidates.description: After foreclosure, withdraw(account, proof) computes accountMerkleRoot = merkleRoot(account, 5 + LOG2_LEAVES_PER_ACCOUNT, 5, hashBlock, hashPair). merkleRoot accepts any account.length <= 2^(5+L) and hashBlock zero-fills the missing tail of the last block and every block past the data. The root therefore does not bind the account's length: every byte string that equals the committed account slot up to trailing zero bytes (shorter, or longer up to the slot size) yields the same accountMerkleRoot and passes the accounts-drive proof at the same accountIndex. withdraw then marks _withdrawn[accountIndex] and executes buildWithdrawalOutput(account) on the attacker-chosen variant. The interface fixes the owner as the last 20 bytes of the account and only recommends a length check; for a builder that accepts more than one account size, appending zero bytes moves the 'last 20 bytes' onto padding (owner = a truncated/zero address) and the real owner's one-time withdrawal is consumed. With the shipped UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder (LibUsdAccount.decode requires exactly 32 bytes) the variants revert, so the default deployment is not affected.
candidates.trigger: Any address, after the guardian forecloses the application and someone proves the accounts-drive root: front-runs or pre-empts the owner with withdraw(account || 0x00..00, sameProof) (or a zero-truncated account), for an application whose withdrawal output builder accepts variable-length accounts as IWithdrawalOutputBuilder permits.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on-chain with released contracts for any Dave application deployed with a custom withdrawal builder that accepts several account sizes. Not reachable with the shipped USD builder (exact 32-byte check). Needs no hash break: the Merkle proof is the honest one for the committed slot.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a public withdraw call by an arbitrary party, not an API caller or a deployment violating A1-A8; but the withdrawal/foreclosure path is not part of the PRT dispute the model describes, and the harm depends on an application-chosen builder, which could be read as 'An application that is not correctly designed ... That exclusion covers only what such an application gets'. Reported anyway per the hunter rules. 2. Role: referee model as deployed referee ('Dave ... and the cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 it pins (input box, output validation) | Referee model, as the deployed referee'). 3. High/Medium cases: none fits; R9's 'lost lengths' clause applies to 'every tree the emulator defines', and the accounts-drive tree is the machine tree read by an application-specific encoding, so R9 does not literally apply. 4. Critical: the section-1 soundness definition is 'a proof verifier accepts a node that the committed tree does not hold at the stated index and height'. The node (accountMerkleRoot at accountIndex, height L) IS held; what is lost is the data-to-node length binding, so the definition is not met. A5 governs outputs proven through the outputs tree, not withdrawal outputs built by the contract. No rule is violated at a reachable state. 5. Low: a real defect (a Merkle verifier that loses the length of the data it authenticates) that violates no rule of this model.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal of section 1 for PRT settlement. It is a data-to-node ambiguity in a pinned Merkle verifier: the contract accepts byte strings the committed state does not hold (only their zero-padded image), and lets an arbitrary party consume an account's one-time withdrawal with them when the builder tolerates the length.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: LibKeccak256.hashBlock allocates a zero-filled block for partial or absent blocks; LibBinaryMerkleTree.merkleRoot only requires data.length <= 2^log2DriveSize; Application.withdraw keys _withdrawn by proof.accountIndex and passes the caller's account bytes to the builder; LibUsdAccount.decode enforces ACCOUNT_SIZE == 32 (so the default builder is safe). No chain run.
candidates.test_idea: Forge test against Application with a WithdrawalConfig (L = 1, 64-byte accounts) and a mock builder that accepts lengths 52 and 64 and decodes the owner from the last 20 bytes: drive root = machine template containing account A (52 bytes, zero-padded to 64) at index 0; foreclose; proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot; call withdraw(A || 12 zero bytes, proof) and assert it reverts (required: the verifier must bind the account length, e.g. by requiring account.length == 2^(5+L) or by hashing the length), then assert withdraw(A, proof) by the owner still succeeds.

not_covered: No new EVM or chain experiments: Dave Commitment/Tree/Match/Tournament, the regenerated step (AccessLogs, Buffer, Memory, SendCmioResponse, UArchReset, EmulatorCompat), LibMachineValidityProof/LibLeafProof/LibOutputValidityProof/LibBinaryMerkleTree and the withdrawal path were checked by reading only.

Checked by reading and found sound (no candidate): Commitment.getRoot/getRootForLastLeaf (sibling count == height; position bits above height are ignored but every caller derives position < 2^height: divergencePosition - 1 from bisection), Match.advanceBisection/sealDivergence invariants (leftmost divergence, runningLeafPosition matches the path, leaves only at height 0, finalStateOne != finalStateTwo), joinTournament/requireFinalState and validContestedFinalState/_parentCommitment (A1: uarch claim last leaf at index 2^38-1 must equal a contested state; winner mapped by final state), winLeafMatch agreeCycle/counter derivation, CartesiStateTransition masks and exact proof consumption, Buffer.peekRoot fixed sibling count (59 - log2size) with stride range check, revert-root-hash leaf (keccak of 32-byte data), rx-buffer region alignment, TLB slot index range check, misaligned-access refusals.

Checked and found sound: LibLeafProof (59 siblings, index < 2^59, keccak(32-byte block) leaves), 0.15.0 constants and getBytes8FromBytes32AtOffset/isYieldedManualWith used by the machine validity proof, LibOutputValidityProof (63 siblings, index < 2^63), proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot (proof length 64 - drive size, start index range guaranteed by LibWithdrawalConfig.isValid).

Checked and found sound: PRT referee model prt.lua validate_claim_response / validate_seal_response / validate_bisection_response / open_uarch_tournament / new_match / advance_bisection against Dave, game-output.lua machine-word and output proofs, cartesi.hash-tree verify_slice/roll_hash_up_tree (sibling count enforced, callers fix target_address exactly or range-check it), 2-argument cartesi.keccak256 rejecting non-32-byte operands.

Checked and found sound: C++ off-chain verifiers (uarch_replay_state_access address/size/type checks, access::make_proof sibling-count and data-size checks, replay_send_cmio_state_access rx write, hash_tree_proof bubble_up), and the out-of-scope main-processor step log page/sibling recomputation (page indices >= 2^52 are rejected as unconsumed pages).
libcmt merkle.c (v0.18.1-test1, cloned) was read, not differentially tested against a naive tree; rollup-http-server and the rollup CLI output-root paths were not examined.

cartesi.hash-tree frontier(last_proof) does not check that the given proof's right-side siblings are pristine (i.e. that it really is the last output); only used with the player's own data (support), not pursued.
